---
title: "How do I import a CSV and confirm the fields were read correctly?"
---

## Immediate answer

To load your own CSV in RStudio, you can use `d <- read.csv(file.choose())` and select the file. The self-contained example below first creates a temporary CSV from recorded `iris` data so that it runs without a file you must download.

```{r setup-quick-import-csv, include=FALSE}
knitr::read_chunk('../examples/import_csv.R')
```

```{r quick-import-csv}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true
```

## What to change

For a real file, replace the demo's `read.csv(csv_file)` with `read.csv(file.choose())`, or supply its actual full path. Use your own data-frame name instead of `d` if that is clearer. Do not assume the file is in the working directory. This worked example writes a **temporary copy of an existing R dataset**; it is not a newly observed study.

## What to check

After loading, run `names(d)` to see the exact column names and `str(d)` for types. Run `dim(d)` and `colSums(is.na(d))` for rows, columns and missing entries. Unexpected blank columns, commonly named `X`, `X.1` and similar, may mean the CSV had extra delimiters; inspect the original before deciding to remove anything. R's `?help` does not automatically know what an arbitrary CSV variable means.

## Complete walkthrough (optional)

The next example runs the same native `read.csv()` operation, then checks that the file exists and inspects the imported structure. The displayed code is also the script you can edit with `ru_edit("import_csv")`.

```{r setup-worked-import-csv, include=FALSE}
knitr::read_chunk('../examples/import_csv.R')
```

```{r worked-import-csv}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true
```

## Interpretation

An imported table is not necessarily a correctly sampled population. R's guessed column types may need checking; converting factor codes or non-numeric text blindly is unsafe. If the file cannot be found, check its location before calculating a statistic.

## Retention practice (optional)

Without copying the complete example, use `write.csv(mtcars, tempfile(fileext=".csv"),row.names=FALSE)` to create a separate practice file, then import it with `read.csv()` and explain how you verified rows, columns and types. Or choose an existing permitted local CSV in RStudio.
